To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fusion of small unil-amellar vesicles onto self-assembled monlayers of thiolipopetides can be optimized by lateral mixing of a thiolipopepide with a lateral spacer, and that this process is accompanied by vesicle adsorption rather than fusion.
the formation of mixed monolayers of the two peptides, I and III, results in an optimum with respect to the formation of lipid bilayers on the surface.
The formation of lipid vesicles onto self-assembled monomolecular layers of a thiolipopeptidic spacer is a function of the spacer composition and the mixing ratio of the spacer with the thiolipid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of supported bilayer lipid membranes by the self-assembly of thiolipids on a gold surface.
the development of a novel approach to create lipid bilayer membranes on gold substrates by using a mixed monolayer of thiolipids and spacer molecules as a template.
the development of a method for forming lipid bilayers by fusion of small unil-amellar vesicles (SUVs) on mixed self-assembled thiolipopeptid monolayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mixed SAMs were not able to form a lipid bilayer, but that the vesicles were fused onto the monolayer.
the thiolipids are not suitable for the preparation of lipid bilayers by the fusion of liposomes.
vesicle fusion is a difficult process to study and that the results presented here are a step forward in the understanding of the process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best conditions to obtain a lipid bilayer on a mixed monolayer were obtained at a mixing ratio of 0.5, where the homogeneity of the monolayer was best and where the lipid bilayer had the best electrical properties.
the best results are obtained for mixed monolayers of the two thiolipopeptidic compounds, and that the optimum is obtained for a mixing ratio of 0.5, i.e., 50% of each component.
the thiolipid I is not an appropriate anchor for the fusion of vesicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of a true lipid bilayers on mixed SAMs is a very difficult task, and it is not clear that this is a useful goal for biosensing applications.
a mixed monolayer of thiolipids and a lateral spacer can form a homogeneous film with respect to the lipid vesicles.
a mixed SAM of thiolipids is an effective way of controlling membrane formation and properties, and that a combination of different methods can be used to characterize the resulting membranes.
